questions.question: An object has a mass of 5 kg and is accelerated at 3 m/s². What is the net force acting on it?
questions.explanation: Using F = ma: F = 5 kg × 3 m/s² = 15 N.
steps: 1. Recall Newton's second law: F = ma.
2. Identify mass m = 5 kg and acceleration a = 3 m/s².
questions.fastStrategy: F = ma is the fundamental equation; multiply mass and acceleration.

questions.question: If an object is thrown upward with an initial velocity of 20 m/s, how long does it take to reach the maximum height? (Use g = 10 m/s²)
questions.explanation: At maximum height, velocity = 0. Using v = u − gt: 0 = 20 − 10t → t = 2 s.
steps: 1. At maximum height, final velocity v = 0.
2. Use kinematic equation: v = u − gt.
questions.fastStrategy: At max height, velocity = 0; use v = u − gt to find time.

questions.question: Two forces act on an object: 12 N to the right and 5 N to the left. What is the net force?
questions.explanation: Net force = 12 N (right) − 5 N (left) = 7 N to the right.
steps: 1. Identify forces: 12 N right, 5 N left.
3. Direction follows the larger force: right.
questions.fastStrategy: Subtract opposing forces; direction is toward the larger force.
